title: Kast’s Search for a Security Breakthrough in Chile
gist: Chile's President Kast, elected on a crime agenda, has seen his own constitutional security reform fail and his approval fall to 26%, as transnational gangs such as the PCC and Tren de Aragua push up kidnapping and extortion even though homicides are down. He now backs a minimalist cross-party reform while aligning Chile with regional and U.S. anti-cartel initiatives.

insights.claim: Chile's national homicide rate fell from a 2022 peak of 6.8 per 100,000 inhabitants to 5.4 in 2025, while kidnappings, extortion, robbery and drug trafficking became more common, according to the Public Prosecutor's Office.
insights.speaker: GRACIELA IBÁÑEZ
insights.so_what: Headline homicide data understates the deterioration in Chile's security. Watch extortion and kidnapping trends instead.

themes.theme: Kast's political cost and reform setbacks

insights.claim: A poll found the share of Chileans who think crime is more violent than a year ago rose 14 points to 68%, and President Kast's approval fell to 26% in the last week of October 2026, his lowest since taking office.
insights.speaker: GRACIELA IBÁÑEZ
insights.so_what: Low approval weakens Kast's legislative capital for security and economic reforms alike.

insights.claim: Kast's constitutional security reform, criticized for letting the president declare states of emergency for up to 240 days without Congress and for expanding the military's policing role, was withdrawn in early October 2026 for lack of support.
insights.speaker: GRACIELA IBÁÑEZ
insights.so_what: Kast's hard-line agenda is constrained by Congress. Expect watered-down, consensus measures.
insights.locator: In August, Kast announced an Agenda

insights.claim: Security minister Trinidad Steinert presented priorities to Congress but issued no formal plan before being replaced in a May cabinet shuffle.
insights.speaker: GRACIELA IBÁÑEZ
insights.so_what: Execution slippage and turnover in the security portfolio are a sign of weak policy delivery.
insights.locator: Kast set out to address that

insights.claim: A cross-party constitutional security reform backed by Kast treats organized crime as contrary to human rights, requires high-risk inmates to be held separately, and expands emergency powers for imminent threats. It needs 29 of 50 Senate votes and then lower-house approval, possibly in 2027.
insights.speaker: GRACIELA IBÁÑEZ
insights.so_what: The timeline for passage stretches into 2027, so near-term security improvements are uncertain.
insights.locator: After failing to pass his own

insights.claim: Senator Araya, a co-author, calls the new reform fairly minimalist and expects Congress to approve it by year-end, which is more optimistic than the article's suggestion that the process may run into next year.
insights.speaker: GRACIELA IBÁÑEZ
insights.so_what: Watch Senate vote timing. A minimalist bill may pass but have limited effect.

insights.claim: Kast launched the Compromiso de Santiago with Argentina, Bolivia, Ecuador and Peru in May 2026 to coordinate on security, financial intelligence, migration and borders. It has since added Paraguay and Uruguay.
insights.speaker: GRACIELA IBÁÑEZ
insights.so_what: An emerging right-leaning South American security bloc may deepen financial-intelligence sharing.

insights.claim: In September 2026, Chile joined Trump's Shield of the Americas but has not decided whether to join the operational Americas Counter Cartel Coalition (A3C) backed by U.S. Southern Command. Defense Minister Fernando Barros reportedly favors observer status for now.
insights.speaker: GRACIELA IBÁÑEZ
insights.so_what: Chile is hedging between U.S. security alignment and sovereignty concerns. Watch the A3C decision.
